title: IBM adds governed agent identities and short-lived credentials
dek: Agent Identity and HashiCorp Vault address delegated authority, revocation and visibility for AI agents operating across business systems.
evidence: IBM product announcement; feature availability varies by component
takeaway: Model each agent as a distinct principal with scoped, expiring credentials, not a shared service account.

sections.title: Context

bullets.detail: A background agent needs its own principal, purpose and revocation path; borrowing an employee's blanket permissions makes audit trails ambiguous.

paragraphs: Agents outgrow shared API keys: A background agent needs its own principal, purpose and revocation path; borrowing an employee's blanket permissions makes audit trails ambiguous.

sections.title: What's new

bullets.detail: IBM introduced managed agent ownership and delegated authority, combined with HashiCorp Vault's short-lived machine credentials, rotation and revocation.
The announcement also covers agent discovery, testing and isolation integrations; some features remain in preview rather than full production availability.

paragraphs: Agent Identity plus Vault: IBM introduced managed agent ownership and delegated authority, combined with HashiCorp Vault's short-lived machine credentials, rotation and revocation.
Broader runtime controls: The announcement also covers agent discovery, testing and isolation integrations; some features remain in preview rather than full production availability.

sections.title: Evidence & limitations

bullets.detail: IBM describes capabilities, but provides no independent measurement of prevented privilege escalations or reduced incident rates.
The identity registry alone cannot enforce scope: every downstream tool and API must check the acting agent and permission at execution time.

paragraphs: Product announcement, not attack study: IBM describes capabilities, but provides no independent measurement of prevented privilege escalations or reduced incident rates.
Enforcement is distributed: The identity registry alone cannot enforce scope: every downstream tool and API must check the acting agent and permission at execution time.

sections.title: Why it matters

bullets.detail: Issue least-privilege, expiring credentials with clear owners and per-action logs. Avoid shared long-lived service tokens.
Revoke authorization between planning and tool execution; verify cached credentials and delegated subagents fail closed.

paragraphs: Treat agents as distinct principals: Issue least-privilege, expiring credentials with clear owners and per-action logs. Avoid shared long-lived service tokens.
